model: M=diag(1,2), |tau1|<=1/10, |tau2|<=1/5; no gravity, friction or disturbance
obstacle: z=q1-q2<=4/5; normalized configuration coordinates, not physical collision geometry
relative_acceleration_bound: z''=tau1-tau2/2>=-1/5 for every admissible torque, regardless of task preservation
derivation: Twice integrate z''>=-1/5: z(t)>=z0+zdot0*t-t^2/10. At t=2 this exceeds obstacle bound. Comparison/integration is hand-derived, not a kernel ODE theorem.

single_instant_derivative_gate.result: Instantaneous first-order derivative inequality passes at a nonviable state. This does not refute control-barrier invariance theorems, which require appropriate all-time feasible dynamics hypotheses.

scalar_sharp_criterion: For scalar z'' freely selectable in[-a,a], half-line z<=B and initial vz>=0, viability iff z+vz^2/(2a)<=B. Necessity from double integration; sufficiency brake -a for vz/a then0. Additional task, lower bounds or actuator coupling can invalidate sufficiency without changing necessity.
task_authority: Safe variations are irrelevant only if excluded from the authoritative task. A specified joint posture makes these same variations task-relevant; an x-only task controller cannot silently replace that request.
evidence: Exact rational arithmetic plus reviewed hand differential comparison. No CBF solver, physical robot or universal controller theorem.
